label: UGC NET June 2026 Paper 2 — Probability questions not in the 1–50 set (booklet numbers not known; identified by official question ID)

items.stem: Let f(x) = (1/2)e^(−|x|), −∞ < x < ∞. Then E(|X|) and Var(|X|) are, respectively,
items.explanation: Idea: the Laplace density is symmetric about 0, so |X| folds the two halves together into a standard exponential distribution. Its mean and variance are both 1. Working: For the standard Laplace density, |X| has pdf e^(−y), y > 0 (Exponential with mean 1), so E|X| = 1 and Var|X| = 1. Official answer: A (1, 1).

items.stem: The moment generating function of a random variable X is given by Mₓ(t) = e^(2t(1+t)). The fourth order central moment of the distribution should be:
items.explanation: Idea: recognise the MGF. e^(μt + σ²t²/2) is the normal MGF, so read off μ and σ², then use the normal fourth central moment, 3σ⁴. Option 12 is the trap of computing 3σ² instead of 3σ⁴. Working: e^(2t + 2t²) = e^(μt + σ²t²/2) with μ = 2, σ² = 4: X ~ N(2, 4), so μ₄ = 3σ⁴ = 48. Official answer: D (48).

items.stem: Let X₁, X₂, …, Xₙ be n iid random variables with mean 1 and variance 4. Then which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: E[(1/(n−1))Σ(Xᵢ − X̄ₙ)²] (printed without its right-hand side; = 4)
items.explanation: Idea: the weak law of large numbers sends a sample average to the population mean of whatever is being averaged. The average of Xᵢ² therefore tends to E(X²), and E(X²) is the variance plus the square of the mean. Working: By the WLLN (1/n)ΣXᵢ² → E(X²) = Var + mean² = 4 + 1 = 5, not 4, so statement 2 is the incorrect one. Source note: Option 4 is printed without its right-hand side; the unbiased sample variance has expectation 4, so it is a correct statement either way. Official answer: B ((1/n)ΣXᵢ² →ᵖ 4).

items.stem: Let X and Y be jointly distributed random variables with joint pdf f(x, y) = (1/4)(1 + cy) for |x| < 1, |y| < 1, and 0 otherwise. Then A. X and Y are independent B. f(x) = 1/2; −1 < x < 1 C. X² and Y² are independent D. E(X²Y²) = 1/9 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Idea: find the marginals by integrating out the other variable, then compare their product with the joint density. Squaring removes the sign of x and y, which is why X² and Y² can be independent even when X and Y are not. Working: Key B, C, D holds for the standard form f(x,y) = (1/4)(1 + xy): f(x) = 1/2, X and Y dependent, X² and Y² independent, E(X²Y²) = 1/3·1/3 = 1/9. Source note: As printed, the density is (1/4)(1 + cy), which factorises as (1/2)·(1 + cy)/2, so X and Y would be independent and all four statements true; no option would then be correct. The official key (B, C, D) matches the standard textbook form (1/4)(1 + xy), which is almost certainly what was intended. Official answer: B (B, C, D only).
